summary: A Fox News roundup of celebrity parents who take a firmer, tough-love approach to raising kids in Hollywood. Arnold Schwarzenegger recalls his "drill instructor" methods and Reese Witherspoon says kids should learn from failure. Daniel Craig, Freddie Prinze Jr. and Sarah Michelle Gellar, Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis, Candace Cameron Bure, and Kristen Bell and Dax Shepard also share rules and strategies to keep their kids grounded and grateful.
one_line: Celebrity parents including Arnold Schwarzenegger and Reese Witherspoon describe strict, tough-love parenting meant to teach resilience, gratitude and discipline.
key_facts: Arnold Schwarzenegger, 76, admitted to People that he had a "drill instructor" approach when his kids were young.

Schwarzenegger said he burned his daughter Katherine's shoes in front of her after she left them by the fireplace three times; Katherine now uses the same methods with her daughters Lyla (3) and Eloise, whom she shares with husband Chris Pratt.
Schwarzenegger threw his son Patrick's mattress off the balcony after Patrick didn't make his bed, and installed a timer that turned the shower ice-cold to limit shower time.
On "The Howard Stern Show," Schwarzenegger warned that over-pampering could be "creating a generation of wimps and weak people."
Reese Witherspoon said on the "Good Inside with Dr. Becky" podcast that parents shouldn't stop letting kids fail, noting her own parents let her sit in discomfort after detention and a suspension.
Witherspoon told her daughter after a lost basketball game, "Maybe you're not good at basketball?" and said it is important to learn what you're not good at.

Daniel Craig told Saga Magazine in 2020 he wants to give away his money before he dies and doesn't want to leave great sums to the next generation; he later called inheritance "distasteful" to Candis magazine.
Freddie Prinze Jr. told Us Weekly in 2021, "We are strict as hell," while Sarah Michelle Gellar has "100 rules" for their kids, now 13 and 11, including no phones at the dinner table.
Mila Kunis said on "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert" in 2020 that she tells her kids Wyatt and Dmitri that Mommy and Daddy are "broke all the time" and that they won't be "entitled a--holes."
Candace Cameron Bure told L.A. Parent she sets firm boundaries with "love and grace" and wants to meet the parents before her kids visit a friend's house.
Kristen Bell told Self in 2020 that her daughters Lincoln and Delta share a bedroom to build character, and that screens are banned during the week but allowed on weekends.
